Mr. Mohammad Rezaul Karim, Advocate, For the accused-petitioner. 
Mr. Md. Fazlur Rahman Khan, D.A.G., For the opposite party No. 1. 
Mr. Md. Aminul Islam, Advocate, For the opposite party No. 2.
parties:
Mosammat Nazma Akter
Vs.
The State and another.
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Sessions Case No. 1630 of 2013 arising out of C.R. Case No. 223 of 2013 (Kotwali Zone) under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act (amended), 1881, now pending in the Court of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the opposite party No. 2, as complainant filed C.R. Case No. 266 of 2013 in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong against the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act on 20.02.2013 stating, inter-alia, that out of good relationship the accused-petitioner took Tk. 50,00,000/= (fifty Lac ) as loan from the opposite party No. 2 for a period of one month and thereafter, the accused-petitioner in order to pay the loan amount issued a cheque of Taka fifty Lac being cheque No. 3481002 dated 29.08.2012 in favour of the complainant-opposite party No. 2, who for the last time placed the said cheque on 26.11.2012 in his account at Brack Bank Ltd. Jubile Road Branch for encashment and the cheque was returned unpaid with endorsement "payment stooped by drawer" and thereafter, the complainant-opposite party finding no other way published a legal notice as per provision of section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act in a daily newspaper namely "Dainik Amader Chattagram" on 24.12.2012 asking to pay the cheque's amount within 30 days but the accused-petitioner did not turn to pay the cheque's amount and thus, he is liable for the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. 

 4. Ultimately, the case was transmitted to the Court of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong for trial, who by his order dated 20.08.2014 framed charge against the accused-petitioner under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. Thereafter, the complainant as PW-1 deposed before the trial court on 02.02.2014. 

 6. Mr. Mohammad Rezaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the accused petitioner did not get any legal notice and he had no knowledge about the matter before filing the case. He further submits that as per mandatory provision of section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act there are 3 alternative ways for serving notice upon the accused, that is : a) by delivering it to the person on whom it is to be served, or (b) by sending it by registered post with acknowledgement due to that person at his usual and last known place of abode or business in Bangladesh; or (c) by publication in a Daily Bangla national newspaper having wide circulation and in this case the complaint published Legal Notice through a local newspaper namely "Dainik Amader Chattagram" which is not a wide circulated Daily Bangla national newspaper and as such, the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed. The learned Advocate to fortify his argument has relied on an unreported judgment of this Court dated 03.07.2014 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 29111 of 2013. 

 7. Mr. Aminul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant-opposite party No. 2 in the course of his argument after placing the petition of complaint as well as counter affidavit submits that the complainant-opposite party No. 2 published Legal Notice through the daily national newspaper namely "Dainik Amader Chattagram" which is a wide circulated Bangla national newspaper and it is on record that the complainant filed the case after exhausting all the legal formalities. 

 10. To appreciate the submission of the learned Advocates for both the side from a correct angle, we have carefully studied the provisions of section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act to the best of our ability and find the provision with regard to serve notice in a well circulated Bangla national newspaper is merely directory and not mandatory, since there is no legal mandate to stop or dismiss the case, if notice is not served through a Bangla national newspaper having wide circulation. Moreover, Mr. Aminul Islam the learned Advocate for the complainant-opposite party argues with force that the complainant-opposite party published his legal notice "Doinik Amader Chattagram" which is a wide circulated daily Bangla national newspaper. The very correctness of fact whether "Doinik Amader Chattagram" is a wide circulated daily Bangla national newspaper or not is a disputed question of fact to be ascertained at the trial on taking evidence and when evidence is required to settle the dispute, the proceeding cannot be quashed. 

 11. On a reading of the petition of complaint it is difficult to hold that there is any legal bar or the continuation of the impugned proceeding will amount to an abuse of the process of the Court. Further, the proposition of law is by now well settled that on the basis of the defence plea or materials, the criminal proceedings should not be stifled before trial, when there is a prima-facie case for going to the trial. 

 12. Taking into consideration of all these aspects of the case as well as principle of law, we are of the view that the petition of complaint undoubtedly discloses that the accused petitioner is liable for the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act and as such, the question of quashing the proceeding does not arise at all. In framing charge, the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong did not commit any illegality whatsoever. Whether a proceeding under section 56IA of the Code Criminal Procedure is to be quashed depends upon the facts of the case itself. 

 14. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. Since this petty case has been dragging for over a period of 4 years, the trial Court concerned is directed to proceed with the case expeditiously in accordance with law.
